region.name: ACH Pipeline Cut-over
region.summary: Planning, execution, load testing, retrospective, and follow-up commitments for migrating ACH processing from Sidekiq to the Go ach-originator pipeline with Pillar Bank, including triage runbooks, Sidekiq decommissioning, NACHA-cutoff alert tuning, and related Q4 engineering and SOC 2 tracking.

brief.text:
The ACH Pipeline Cut-over region covers Stencil's migration of ACH origination and return processing off Rails/Sidekiq workers onto the Go ach-originator service, as defined in ADR-024 and its approved design doc. The trigger was the April 6 P0 incident, where Sidekiq workers failed during the Sunday batch. Pillar Bank is the originating bank partner, and its requirements shaped the timeline and rollback hold. The original target was end of June 2026. The June 27 load test failed at 3x volume because of outbox vacuum contention. After fixes, the July runs passed at 3x and 4x, and the cut-over slipped to and was executed on 2026-08-18. In the 2026 architecture inventory, ach-originator sits alongside the other Go services (brokerd and the notification service), the Rails monolith, the iOS and Android apps, and the experiments platform. The load test report template records what was tested, the pass criteria, results per volume multiplier, a pass / fail / pass-with-conditions decision, and follow-ups. A later September run showed brokerd funding and orders passing at 3x projected GA-week volume, with a p99 funding call of 210ms.

Operationally, the region includes a first-five-minutes SEV1 triage runbook for when no ACH file has been submitted for the current window. The steps are to acknowledge the page, check the dashboard, post in the incident channel, and then check three things. First, check leader election, which uses a Postgres advisory lock. Second, look for entries stuck in pending, which points to the SQS relay. Third, look for entries stuck in packaged, which points to SFTP submission to Pillar Bank.

The retro found several things went well. The cut-over itself was smooth, the shadow diff caught the only real bug, the June slip paid off, and Sarah Kim ramped quickly. The problems were an R03 returns-mapping bug caught in shadow mode, dashboard lag, a noisy NACHA-cutoff alert, and too much load on Marcus. Retro decisions made Sarah Kim the secondary pipeline owner. They also kept the Sidekiq ACH path dormant through a 30-day rollback hold ending 2026-09-17, after which it is to be deleted. Eng Staff approved that deletion conditional on no incidents during the hold. Eng Staff also froze growth experiments touching onboarding, deposits, or round-ups from Sep 8 until investing GA plus two weeks. They flagged that the first DriveWealth corporate action during beta had never been exercised in sandbox. Their action items cover beta metrics, the ACH decommission plan, a SOC 2 readiness review, and unfreeze criteria.

The Q4 engineering commitments checklist assigns owners and absolute October 2026 deadlines. The commitments are the position reconciliation fix, Android parity for investing screens, go/no-go #2, deleting the Sidekiq ACH code, NACHA-cutoff alert tuning, idempotency keys for money-moving jobs, and locking the Q4 plan. Open attention items include a risk around the first Sunday peak on the new pipeline. Code review norms are also tracked: link PRs to the ADRs or customer issues they implement, and push back on "I need to merge this today" author pressure. One reflection called the incident period the worst engineering day of the author's Stencil tenure while noting the team handled it well. Typical questions this region answers include why the cut-over slipped, when Sidekiq ACH code gets deleted, how to triage a missed ACH submission window, who owns the pipeline, what load test results were, and what follow-ups remain open.

items.title: Decision: Keep Sidekiq ACH path dormant then delete
items.summary: Keep the Sidekiq ACH path deployable but dormant until the 30-day hold ends on 2026-09-17, then delete it.
